Graphing exercise using publicly available data of spending on children in the United States from 1997 through 2016. Data is courtesy of the TidyTuesday [^1] and the Urban Institute.[^2]

[^1]: Harmon, Jon (2020, September 15). *US Spending on Kids*. TidyTuesday. <https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/blob/main/data/2020/2020-09-15/readme.md>

[^2]: Urban Institute (2020, August 18). *State-by-State Spending on Kids*. Urban Data Catalog. <https://datacatalog.urban.org/dataset/state-state-spending-kids-dataset>

```{r}
#| out-width: 70%
#| fig-align: center
#| fig-alt: "Four line charts showing national spending on children in different areas."

library(tidyverse)

#Borrowed from TidyTuesday instructions
kids <- readr::read_csv('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday/main/data/2020/2020-09-15/kids.csv')

national_average <- kids |>
  group_by(year, variable) |>
  
  #Isolate four categories of interest
  filter(variable == "lib" |
         variable == "PK12ed" |
         variable == "Medicaid_CHIP" |
         variable == "parkrec") |>
  summarize(inf_adj_perchild = mean(inf_adj_perchild)) |>
  mutate(
    variable = recode(variable,
      lib = "Libraries",
      PK12ed = "PreK–12 Education",
      Medicaid_CHIP = "Medicaid/CHIP",
      parkrec = "Parks & Recreation"
    )
  )

ggplot(national_average, aes(x = year, y = inf_adj_perchild)) +
  geom_line(aes(color = variable)) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable) +
  labs(
    title = "National Spending on Children by Year",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Spending Per Child (Inflation Adjusted in Billions $)"
  ) +
  
  #Centered format
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```
